references.text: The Lord God opens the ear of the servant so that he listens and does God's will, a motif reflected in Jesus' submission to the Father's will in John 6:38.
In an earlier chapter of the same Gospel, Jesus confirms that he does not seek his own will but the will of the one who sent him, which is a direct theological precursor to the statement in 6:38.
Jesus defines his bread as doing the will of the one who sent him, a direct parallel to the motif of having come down from heaven to carry out this will.
Jesus confirms that his message and actions are the Father's will, and that he has not spoken on his own authority, underscoring the theme of having come down from heaven to do God's will.
The psalm referred to in Hebrews describes the Messiah as coming to do God's will, a theme central to Jesus' self-understanding in John 6:38.
